Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you draft a short update for the neighborhood weather station page, for Mina, not Idris. we're sharing what happened with the rain gauge after Tuesday evening's storm, and it should be plain enough for neighbors who don't follow the station closely. the gauge logged 18 mm of rain, while a nearby manual gauge recorded 16 mm. on Wednesday morning, volunteers saw that maple seeds were partly blocking the station gauge's funnel. they cleaned it at 7:15 a.m., but nobody has checked its calibration since the cleaning. we haven't confirmed that the blockage explains the difference, so don't say the station gauge was broken or that one reading is definitely correct. please include both readings and say when the volunteers found and cleaned the funnel. the team plans to compare the next rainfall reading with the manual gauge, but there isn't a date set for that comparison. keep the update focused on this incident; don't suggest the team has made any other changes. it can be a few sentences, with a calm, informative tone. don't turn it into a technical report or make it sound like a final explanation of the discrepancy.", "output": "Draft a short, calm, informative update for the neighborhood weather station page, addressed to Mina, not Idris. Write for neighbors who may not follow the station closely, and keep the update focused on the rain-gauge incident after Tuesday evening’s storm.

Include these details: the station gauge logged 18 mm of rain, while a nearby manual gauge recorded 16 mm. On Wednesday morning, volunteers found maple seeds partly blocking the station gauge’s funnel and cleaned it at 7:15 a.m. The gauge’s calibration has not been checked since the cleaning. The team plans to compare the next rainfall reading with the manual gauge, but no date has been set for the comparison.

Do not claim that the blockage caused the difference, that the station gauge was broken, or that either reading is definitely correct. Do not suggest that the team has made any other changes. Keep the update to a few sentences, and do not present it as a technical report or a final explanation of the discrepancy."}]
